definitionBean.title: Sector
definitionBean.definition: The region bounded by two radii drawn from the center of a circle and the arc between them is called a sector.
definitionBean.explanation: Area of the sector = (θ/360°) × πr², and Length of the arc = (θ/360°) × 2πr, where θ is the central angle and r is the radius.

definitionBean.title: Segment
definitionBean.definition: The region bounded by a chord of a circle and its corresponding arc is called a segment.
definitionBean.explanation: Area of the minor segment = area of the sector - area of the corresponding triangle. Area of the major segment = area of the whole circle - area of the minor segment.
importantPoints: Minor segment = sector Area - triangle Area
Major segment = of the circle Area - Minor segment
A chord divides a circle into two segments

definitionBean.title: Combined Figures / Areas of Combined Plane Figures
definitionBean.definition: When two or more geometric figures (such as circles, sectors, triangles, and rectangles) form a combined figure, its area is found by adding or subtracting the areas of all parts.
definitionBean.explanation: For combined figures, first identify each part (circle, square, sector, etc.) separately, then calculate their areas using the appropriate formulas and add or subtract them as required.
importantPoints: First identify all parts of the figure separately
Find the area of each part using its appropriate formula
Finally, add or subtract to find the total area

parts.statement: Find the area of a sector of a circle with radius 6 cm and angle 60°. (Take π = 22/7.)
parts.explanation:
Given:
Radius (r) = 6 cm
Central angle (θ) = 60°

Area of the sector = (θ / 360°) × πr²
= (60° / 360°) × (22/7) × (6)²
= (1 / 6) × (22/7) × 36
= (22 × 6) / 7
= 132/7 cm² (or 18.85 cm²)

parts.statement: Find the area of a quadrant of a circle whose circumference is 22 cm. (Take π = 22/7.)
parts.explanation:
Given:
Circumference of the circle = 22 cm
2πr = 22
2 × (22/7) × r = 22
r = (22 × 7) / (2 × 22) = 7/2 cm

Angle of the quadrant (θ) = 90°
Area of the quadrant = (90° / 360°) × πr²
= (1 / 4) × (22/7) × (7/2) × (7/2)
= (1 / 4) × (22/7) × (49/4)
= 77/8 cm²

parts.statement: A circle has radius 10 cm and the angle subtended at the center is 90°. Find the area of the corresponding minor sector. (Take π = 3.14.)
A circle has radius 21 cm and the arc subtends an angle of 60° at the center. Find the length of the arc.
A chord of a circle with radius 14 cm subtends an angle of 60° at the center. Find the area of the corresponding minor segment. (Take √3 = 1.73.)
parts.explanation:
Given: r = 14 cm, θ = 60°

1. Area of the sector = (60°/360°) × (22/7) × 14²
= (1/6) × (22/7) × 196 = 308/3 cm² = 102.67 cm²

2. Area of the equilateral triangle = (√3/4) × r²
= (1.73/4) × 14² = 1.73 × 49 = 84.77 cm²

3. Area of the minor segment = Area of the sector - area of the triangle
= 102.67 - 84.77 = 17.90 cm² (approximately)

parts.statement: The minute hand of a clock is 14 cm long. Find the area swept by the hand in 5 minutes.
parts.explanation:
Angle covered by the minute hand in 60 minutes = 360°
Therefore, angle covered in 1 minute = 360° / 60 = 6°
Angle covered in 5 minutes (θ) = 5 × 6° = 30°

Length of the hand (r) = 14 cm
Area swept = (30° / 360°) × (22/7) × (14)²
= (1 / 12) × (22/7) × 196
= (1 / 12) × 616
= 154/3 cm²
